newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bank Danamon down after planned meeting.
newsitem.headline: Bank Danamon down after planned meeting.

text.p: Shares of large Indonesian privately-owned bank, PT Bank Danamon Indonesia, fell on Wednesday after announcement of a proposed extraordinary meeting of shareholders, brokers said.
Bank Danamon was down 50 rupiah, or 4.65 percent, to a year low of 1,025 rupiah, with volume approaching six million shares, at 0430 GMT. It later recovered to 1,050 rupiah.
"Some players were speculating that there might be some negative news coming out from the meeting such as forex losses," one broker with a large local brokerage firm said.
One Bank Danamon official, however, denied the speculation, saying it was baseless, and added that the agenda of the meeting had already been announced.
"It's baseless. It's not true. There are so many rumours coming out from the market. I hear false rumours everyday," Yaduhu Immanuel, an official with the bank's corporate secretary's office, said.
Danamon said earlier it planned to hold an extraordinary shareholders meeting in late August to seek approvals for proposed transactions with subsidiaries.
